paragraphs: City Holding Company (the "Company" or "City Holding" or the "Parent Company") is a financial holding company headquartered in Charleston, West Virginia. The Company conducts its principal activities through its wholly-owned subsidiary, City National Bank of West Virginia ("City National"). City National provides banking, wealth and investment management and other financial solutions through its network of 96 bank branches and 934 full-time equivalent associates located in West Virginia, Kentucky, Virginia and southeastern Ohio. The Company's business activities are currently limited to one reportable business segment, which is community banking.
The principal products produced and services rendered by City National include:

•Commercial Banking - City National offers a full range of commercial banking services to corporations and other business customers. Loans are provided for a variety of business purposes, including financing for commercial and industrial projects, income producing commercial real estate, owner-occupied real estate and construction and land development. City National also provides deposit services for commercial customers, including treasury management, lockbox and other cash management services. City National provides merchant credit card services through an agreement with a third-party vendor.

•Consumer Banking - City National provides banking services to consumers, including checking, savings and money market accounts as well as certificates of deposit and individual retirement accounts. In addition, City National provides consumers with installment and real estate loans and lines of credit. City National also offers credit cards through an agreement with a third-party vendor.

•Mortgage Banking - City National provides mortgage banking services, including fixed and adjustable-rate mortgages, construction financing, land loans, production of conventional and government insured mortgages, secondary marketing and mortgage servicing.

•Wealth and Investment Management Services - City National offers specialized services and expertise in the areas of wealth management, investment and custodial services for commercial and individual customers. These services include the administration of personal trusts and estates, as well as the management of investment accounts for individuals, employee benefit plans and charitable foundations. City National also provides corporate trust and institutional custody, financial and estate planning and retirement plan services.

City National's customer base is diverse, and no single depositor could have a material adverse effect on liquidity, capital, or other elements of financial performance. Although no portion of City National's loan portfolio is concentrated within a single industry or group of related industries in excess of City National's internally designated limit, residential mortgage loans have historically comprised a significant portion of its loan portfolio. At December 31, 2025, approximately 47% of the Company's loan portfolio was categorized as residential mortgage and home equity loans. However, due to the fractured nature of residential mortgage lending, there is no concentration of credits that would be considered materially detrimental to the Company's financial position or operating results. At December 31, 2025, approximately 52% of the Company's loan portfolio was categorized as commercial and industrial and commercial real estate. However, there is no concentration of credits that would be considered materially detrimental to the Company's financial position or operating results.
City National's loan portfolio is comprised of commercial and industrial, commercial real estate, residential real estate, home equity, consumer loans and demand deposit account ("DDA") overdrafts.

City National's commercial and industrial loan portfolio consists of loans to corporate and other legal entity borrowers, primarily small to mid-size industrial and commercial companies. Commercial and industrial loans typically involve a higher level of risk than other loan types, including industry specific risks such as the pertinent economy, new technology, labor rates and cyclicality, as well as customer specific factors, such as cash flow, financial structure, operating controls and asset quality. Collateral securing these loans includes equipment, machinery, inventory, receivables and vehicles. As of December 31, 2025, City National reported $454.0 million of loans classified as "Commercial and Industrial".

Commercial real estate loans consist of commercial mortgages, which generally are secured by nonresidential and multi-family residential properties, including hotel/motel and apartment lending. Commercial real estate loans are provided to many of the same customers and carry similar industry and customer specific risks as the commercial and industrial loans, but
have different collateral risks. As of December 31, 2025, City National reported $1.87 billion of loans classified as "Commercial Real Estate."
In order to group loans with similar risk characteristics, the portfolio is further segmented by product types:

•Commercial 1-4 Family loans consist of residential single-family, duplex, triplex, and fourplex rental properties and totaled $210.2 million as of December 31, 2025. Risk characteristics are driven by rental housing demand as well as economic and employment conditions. These properties exhibit greater risk than multi-family properties due to fewer income sources.
•The Hotel portfolio is comprised of all lodging establishments and totaled $398.6 million as of December 31, 2025. Risk characteristics relate to the demand for business and personal travel.

paragraphs: An investment in the Company's common stock is subject to risks inherent to the Company's business. The material risks and uncertainties that management believes affect the Company are described below. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones facing the Company. Additional risks and uncertainties that management is not aware of or focused on or that management currently deems immaterial may also impair the Company's business operations. You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, before making an investment in the Company's common stock. If any of the following risks occur, the Company's financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected, and you could lose all or part of your investment. In this section, the term "Company" includes City National unless the circumstances dictate otherwise.

The Company's business is concentrated in West Virginia, Kentucky, Virginia and southeastern Ohio. As a result, the Company's results of operation, cash flows and financial condition are affected by local and regional economic conditions. A downturn in the economies within the Company's market areas, or in any one of them, could negatively impact the Company's results of operation and financial condition. Some examples of economic deterioration include declines in economic growth, declines in consumer and business confidence, prolonged increases in inflation, increases in the cost of capital and credit, and limitations in the availability of credit. Trade policies and tariffs could also lead to an uncertain economic environment and increase inflation, reduce consumer spending, or raise the cost of borrowing. The Company's financial performance generally, and the ability of its customers to pay interest on and repay principal of outstanding loans to City National, is highly dependent on the strength of the economic and business environment in the market areas where the Company operates and in the United States as a whole. Additionally, the value of collateral securing loans made and held by City National is impacted by the strength of the economy. Deteriorating economic conditions in the Company's market areas could cause declines in the overall quality of the loan portfolio requiring charge-off of a greater percentage of loans and/or an increase in the allowance for credit losses, which could negatively impact the Company's results of operations and financial condition.

While the economic and business environments in West Virginia, Kentucky, Virginia and southeastern Ohio have shown resilience, there can be no assurance that such resilience and improvement will continue or that the economies in the Company's market areas, or the United States as a whole, will not slip into a recession. A lack of continued economic improvement or economic recession could adversely affect the Company's results of operation and financial condition. An economic slowdown, or an increase in joblessness, whether caused by general economic conditions or the rise of alternative technologies replacing members of the workforce, could have the following consequences:
•Loan delinquencies may increase; •Problem assets and foreclosures may increase; •Demand for City National's products and services may decline; and
•Collateral (including real estate) that secures loans made by City National may decline in value, in turn reducing customers' borrowing power and making existing loans less secure.

The oil, natural gas and coal industries, and businesses ancillary thereto, play an important role in the economies of West Virginia, Kentucky, Virginia and southeastern Ohio. Historic, and ongoing, volatility in oil and gas prices has negatively impacted oil and gas and other businesses in the Company's market areas. Additionally, the coal industry has historically been in decline as a result of increased environmental and safety regulatory burden, increased competition from alternative energy sources and a decline in demand for coal. The Company has limited direct exposure to coal industry specific loans. Prolonged low oil and gas prices, and continued decline in the coal industry, could result in downward pressure on businesses in the Company's market area which could negatively affect City National's customers (both individuals and businesses). As a result, the Company's operating results and financial condition could be negatively impacted.

City Holding Company (the "Company"), a West Virginia corporation headquartered in Charleston, West Virginia, is a registered financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act and conducts its principal activities through its wholly owned subsidiary, City National Bank of West Virginia ("City National"). City National is a retail and consumer-oriented community bank with 96 bank branches in West Virginia (58), Kentucky (22), Virginia (13) and southeastern Ohio (3). City National provides credit, deposit, and wealth and investment management services to its customers in a broad geographical area that includes many rural and small community markets in addition to larger cities including Charleston (WV), Huntington (WV), Martinsburg (WV), Ashland (KY), Lexington (KY), Winchester (VA) and Staunton (VA). In the Company's key markets, the Company's primary subsidiary, City National, often ranks in the top three relative to deposit market share and the top two relative to branch share (Charleston/Huntington MSA, Beckley/Lewisburg counties, Staunton MSA and Winchester, VA/WV Eastern Panhandle counties). In addition to its branch network, City National's delivery channels include automated-teller-machines ("ATMs"), interactive-teller-machines ("ITMs"), mobile banking, debit cards, interactive voice response systems, and internet technology. The Company's business activities are currently limited to one reportable business segment, which is community banking. See Note Three for additional information on the Company's reportable business segment.
CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ESTIMATES

The accounting policies of the Company conform to U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and require management to make estimates and develop assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and related footnotes. These estimates and assumptions are based on information available to management as of the date of the financial statements. Actual results could differ significantly from management's estimates. As this information changes, management's estimates and assumptions used to prepare the Company's financial statements and related disclosures may also change. The most significant accounting policies followed by the Company are presented in Note One of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included herein. Based on the valuation techniques used and the sensitivity of financial statement amounts to the methods, assumptions, and estimates underlying those amounts, management has identified: (i) the determination of the allowance for credit losses and (ii) income taxes accounting to be the accounting areas that require the most subjective or complex judgments and, as such, could be most subject to revision as new information becomes available.

The Allowance for Credit Losses section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K provides management's analysis of the Company's allowance for credit losses and related provision. The allowance for credit losses is a valuation account that is deducted from the loans' amortized cost basis to present the net amount expected to be collected on the loans. Loans are charged off against the allowance when management believes the uncollectibility of a loan balance is confirmed. Expected recoveries do not exceed the aggregate of amounts previously charged-off and expected to be charged-off. Management estimates the allowance balance using relevant available information, from internal and external sources, relating to past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts. Historical credit loss experience provides the basis for the estimation of expected credit losses. Adjustments to historical loss information are made for differences in current loan-specific risk characteristics, such as differences in underwriting standards, portfolio mix, delinquency level, or term as well as for changes in environmental conditions, such as changes in unemployment rates, property values, or other relevant factors. These evaluations are conducted at least quarterly and more frequently if deemed necessary. Additionally, all commercial loans within the portfolio are subject to internal risk grading. Risk grades are generally assigned by the primary lending officer and are periodically evaluated by the Company's internal loan review process.

In evaluating the appropriateness of its allowance for credit losses, the Company stratifies the loan portfolio into six major groupings. The Company has identified the following portfolio segments and measures the allowance for credit losses using the following methods:
Commercial real estate: 1-4 family Migration Hotels Migration Multi-family Migration Non Residential Non-Owner Occupied Migration
Non Residential Owner Occupied Migration Residential real estate Vintage Home equity Vintage

Migration is an analysis that tracks a closed pool of loans for a configurable period of time and calculates a loss ratio on only those loans in the pool at the start date based on outstanding balance. Vintage is a predictive loss model that includes a reasonable approximation of probable and estimable future losses by tracking each loan's net losses over the life of the loan as compared to its original balance. For demand deposit overdrafts, the allowance for credit losses is measured using the historical loss rate. Loans that do not share risk characteristics are evaluated on an individual basis. Loans evaluated individually are not included in the collective evaluation. When management determines that foreclosure is probable, the expected credit losses are based on the fair value of the collateral at the reporting date, adjusted for selling costs as appropriate.

paragraphs: City Holding Company (the "Company" or "City Holding" or the "Parent Company") 為一間財務控股公司，總部設於西維吉尼亞州查爾斯敦。本公司透過其百分之百擁有之子公司 City National Bank of West Virginia ("City National") 進行其主要業務活動。City National 透過位於西維吉尼亞州、肯塔基州、維吉尼亞州及美國俄亥俄州東南部之 96 家分行與 934 名全職等效員工所組成之網路，提供銀行、財富與投資管理及其他金融解決方案。本公司目前之業務活動僅限於一個應報告分部，即社區銀行業務。
City National 所提供之主要產品與服務為：
•商業銀行服務 - City National 向公司與其他商業客戶提供完整之商業銀行服務。貸款用以支援多種商業用途，包括商業與工業項目之融資、產生收入之商業不動產、自用不動產及建設與土地開發。City National 同時為商業客戶提供存款服務，包括財務管理、鎖箱及其他現金管理服務。City National 透過與第三方供應商之協議，提供商家信用卡服務。
•消費者銀行服務 - City National 向消費者提供銀行服務，包括支票帳戶、儲蓄帳戶與貨幣市場帳戶，以及定期存款與個人退休帳戶。此外，City National 同時為消費者提供分期付款與不動產貸款及信用線。City National 透過與第三方供應商之協議，提供信用卡服務。
•房貸銀行服務 - City National 提供房貸銀行服務，包括固定利率與變動利率房貸、建設融資、土地貸款、生產傳統與政府擔保房貸、二次行銷與房貸服務。
•財富與投資管理服務 - City National 向商業與個人客戶提供財富管理、投資與保管服務之專業服務與專業知識。這些服務包括個人信託與遺產之管理，以及為個人、員工福利計畫與慈善基金管理投資帳戶。City National 同時提供公司信託與機構保管、財務與遺產規劃及退休計畫服務。

City National 之客戶羣體多元，單一存款人不會對流動性、資本或其他財務表現要素造成重大不利影響。雖然 City National 之貸款組閤中，無任何部分集中於單一產業或相關產業羣組，且超過 City National 內部所設定之限額，但住宅房貸貸款歷來佔其貸款組合之相當大比例。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司之貸款組合約有 47% 被歸類為住宅房貸與住宅貸款。然而，由於住宅房貸貸款之分散性，並無任何信貸集中會被視為對本公司財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司之貸款組合約有 52% 被歸類為商業與工業及商業不動產。然而，並無任何信貸集中會被視為對本公司財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
City National 之貸款組合包含商業與工業、商業不動產、住宅不動產、住宅貸款、消費者貸款及需求存款帳戶 ("DDA") 溢繳款。

City National 的商業及工業貸款組合包含貸款予企業及其他法律實體借款人，主要是中小型工業及商業公司。商業及工業貸款通常涉及較其他貸款類型更高的風險，包括產業特定風險，例如相關總體經濟、新技術、勞動成本及週期性，以及客戶特定因素，例如現金流、財務結構、營運控制及資產品質。這些貸款的擔保品包括設備、機械、存貨、應收款及車輛。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，City National 報告有 454.0 百萬美元的貸款被歸類為『商業及工業』。
商業不動產貸款包含商業房貸，通常由非住宅及多家庭住宅不動產擔保，包括酒店/旅館及公寓貸款。商業不動產貸款提供給許多與商業及工業貸款相同客戶，並具有相似的產業及客戶特定風險，但
擔保風險不同。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，City National 報告有 1.87 十億美元的貸款被歸類為『商業不動產』。
為將具有相似風險特徵的貸款歸類，組合進一步按產品類型分為以下分部：
•商業 1-4 房貸款包含住宅單戶、雙戶、三戶及四戶出租不動產，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日總計為 210.2 百萬美元。風險特徵由出租住宅需求以及經濟及就業條件所驅動。這些不動產因收入來源較少，相比多家庭不動產具有更高的風險。
•旅館組合包含所有住宿設施，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日總計為 398.6 百萬美元。風險特徵與商務及個人旅行需求有關。

City Holding Company（"本公司"），為西弗吉尼亞州公司，總部設於西弗吉尼亞州查爾斯頓，係依銀行控股公司法註冊之金融控股公司，其主要業務活動係透過其 wholly owned subsidiary，City National Bank of West Virginia（"City National"）進行。City National 為一零售與消費者導向之地方銀行，於西弗吉尼亞州（58）、肯塔基州（22）、維吉尼亞州（13）及美國東部俄亥俄州（3）設有 96 家分行。City National 為其客戶提供信用、存款及財富與投資管理服務，服務範圍涵蓋廣泛地理區域，包括許多鄉村與小型社區市場，以及較大城市，如查爾斯頓（WV）、欣頓（WV）、馬丁斯堡（WV）、阿什蘭（KY）、列剋星敦（KY）、溫徹斯特（VA）及斯塔頓（VA）。在本公司之主要市場，本公司之主要子公司 City National 通常在存款市場佔有率排名前三位，且在分行數量排名前兩位（查爾斯頓/欣頓都會區、貝克利/劉易斯堡縣、斯塔頓都會區及溫徹斯特，VA/WV 東部山區縣）。除分行網路外，City National 之服務通路亦包括自動提款機（"ATMs"）、互動提款機（"ITMs"）、行動銀行、提款卡、互動語音回應系統及網路科技。本公司目前之業務活動僅限於一個應報告分部，即地方銀行業務。有關本公司應報告分部之更多資訊，請參閱第三節附註。
關鍵會計政策與會計估計

本公司之會計政策遵循美國通用會計準則，並要求管理階層必須做出估計及發展假設，以影響財務報表及相關附註中所列示之金額。這些估計及假設係根據管理階層在財務報表日所掌握之資訊進行。實際結果可能與管理階層之估計有顯著差異。隨著資訊變動，管理階層用以編製本公司財務報表及相關揭露之估計及假設亦可能變動。本公司遵循之最重要會計政策，已於本文件所附之綜合財務報表附註第一節中說明。根據所使用之評估技術及財務報表金額對方法、假設及估計之敏感度，管理階層已辨識出：(i) 貸款減損準備之確定，以及 (ii) 所得稅會計為需運用最多主觀或複雜判斷之會計領域，因此，這些領域可能因新資訊之取得而最易修正。

本年度10-K表報表之「貸款減損準備」節提供管理階層對本公司貸款減損準備及相關提列之分析。貸款減損準備為一評估帳戶，用以從貸款之攤銷成本中扣除，以反映預期可收取之貸款淨金額。當管理階層認為貸款餘額無法收回時，將該貸款核銷至減損準備。預期回收金額不超過已核銷金額及預期將核銷金額之總和。管理階層使用與貸款相關之內部及外部來源資訊，包括過往事件、當前狀況及合理且可支持之預測，以估計減損準備金額。歷史信用減損經驗為預期信用減損之估計基礎。對歷史減損資訊進行調整，以反映當前貸款特定風險特徵之差異，例如授信標準之差異、貸款組合結構、逾期程度或期限，以及環境條件之變動，例如失業率、房地產價值或其他相關因素。這些評估至少每季進行一次，若認為必要，則更頻繁進行。此外，所有商業貸款均需接受內部風險等級評估。風險等級通常由主要貸款經理指派，並定期由本公司內部貸款審查程序進行評估。
在評估貸款減損準備是否適當時，本公司將貸款組合區分為六大主要羣組。本公司已辨識出以下組合段落，並使用以下方法衡量貸款減損準備：
商業不動產：1-4 房家庭遷移旅館遷移多家庭遷移非住宅非所有權人佔用遷移
非住宅所有權人佔用遷移住宅不動產古董住宅房貸古董

遷移係指追蹤一筆封閉貸款池於可設定期間內的表現，並僅針對該貸款池在起始日期時點的貸款計算損失比率。古董係指預測性損失模型，包含合理近似未來可能且可估計的損失，透過追蹤每筆貸款在其貸款期間內的淨損失與原始貸款餘額進行比較。對於活期存款透支，信用損失準備係根據歷史損失率衡量。風險特性不相同之貸款，則個別評估。個別評估之貸款不包含於集體評估中。當管理層判斷可能遭強制執行時，預期信用損失係根據報告日期之擔保品公允價值，並適當調整出售成本計算。

本公司高度依賴其管理團隊，且關鍵管理人員的意外流失可能對其營運產生不利影響。

paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股有風險，這些風險與本公司業務內在相關。管理階層認為影響本公司的主要風險與不確定性已於下文描述。下文所述的風險與不確定性並非本公司唯一面臨的風險。此外，管理階層未預見或未特別關注，或目前認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，也可能影響本公司的業務運作。您在考量是否投資本公司普通股前，應仔細審閱下文所述的風險，以及本年度報告表10-K所包含或參考的其他資訊。若任何下列風險發生，可能對本公司的財務狀況與營運成果造成重大且不利的影響，您可能損失全部或部分投資。本節中，"本公司"一詞包括City National，除非情況另有明確說明。

本公司業務集中於西維吉尼亞州、肯塔基州、維吉尼亞州與美國東南部俄亥俄州。因此，本公司營運成果、現金流與財務狀況受當地與區域經濟條件影響。本公司市場區域內經濟衰退，或其中任一區域經濟衰退，都可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成負面影響。經濟惡化的一些例子包括經濟成長減緩、消費者與企業信心下降、通貨膨脹持續上升、資本與信貸成本增加，以及信貸可取得性受到限制。貿易政策與關稅也可能導致經濟環境不確定，提高通貨膨脹，減少消費者支出，或提高借款成本。本公司整體財務表現，以及客戶償還貸款本金與支付貸款利息的能力，高度依賴本公司營運區域與美國整體經濟與商業環境的強度。此外，City National所發放與持有的貸款擔保品價值也受經濟強度影響。本公司營運區域經濟條件惡化，可能導致貸款組合整體品質下降，需要提高貸款核銷比例與/或增加信用損失撥備，這可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成負面影響。
雖然西維吉尼亞州、肯塔基州、維吉尼亞州與美國東南部俄亥Ohio的經濟與商業環境顯示出強韌性，但無法保證這種強韌性與改善會持續，或美國整體經濟與本公司營運區域經濟不會陷入衰退。持續經濟改善不足或經濟衰退，可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。經濟減速，或失業率上升，無論是因一般經濟條件或替代性科技取代勞動力所致，都可能產生以下後果：
•貸款違約率可能上升；•問題資產與法拍物可能增加；•客戶對本公司產品與服務的需求可能下降；
•擔保品（包括不動產）可能價值下降，進而降低客戶借款能力，使現有貸款較不安全。

石油、天然氣與煤炭產業，以及相關產業，對西維吉尼亞州、肯塔基州、維吉尼亞州與美國東南部俄亥Ohio的經濟有重要影響。歷史與持續的石油與天然氣價格波動已對本公司營運區域內的石油、天然氣及其他產業造成負面影響。此外，煤炭產業歷來處於衰退，這是因為環境與安全規範負擔增加、替代能源競爭增加以及煤炭需求下降所致。本公司對煤炭產業特定貸款的直接暴露有限。持續低石油與天然氣價格，以及煤炭產業持續衰退，可能對本公司營運區域內的企業造成下行壓力，進而對City National的客戶（包括個人與企業）造成負面影響。因此，本公司營運成果與財務狀況可能受到負面影響。
